subject: QBR prep — Velocity signals, gating criteria, fallback playbook
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep — Velocity signals, gating criteria, fallback playbook

Team,

As we stitch together the QBR narrative, two things we need to lock this week: (1) a concise velocity signal matrix that shows expected vs. observed throughput for the next three quarters, and (2) a clear, tiered fallback playbook for releases that maps to customer-facing impact levels (P1/P2/P3).

Quick summary of current posture from product/eng: 
- Roadmap: Core 2.1 feature set (chat memory persistence, batching affinity) is feature-complete in design; dev velocity has been uneven across the infra and runtime teams due to a kernel regression we fixed last sprint.
- Timeline: Soft freeze targeted 2028-06-20, hard freeze 2028-07-05, initial canary window 2028-07-12 to 2028-07-16.
- Risk: Two high risks — (A) runtime kernel regression could slip performance tests for seq>4k; (B) dependency on third-party quantization toolchain for Dedicated customers (Novum Health) remains unresolved.

Attached: velocity_signal_matrix.xlsx (draft). Also posted a short doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1QBR-Prep-Velocity-Matrix

Asks: 
1) Monica — can you validate the customer-impact buckets for Novum and Adept? I put them in the matrix as High/Medium respectively.
2) Laura — can you craft a single-slide exec summary of gating criteria (go/no-go signals) we can put in the QBR pack?
3) Rishi — need a concrete fallback playbook (owners + runbook links) by Thursday — I sketched a starter in the attached.

I want a short sync Thursday 10:30 PT — 30m — to accept final artifacts. If that conflicts, propose alternate.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR prep — Velocity signals, gating criteria, fallback playbook

Thanks Marcus — quick clarifications: 
- Novum Health: impact is indeed High for latency-sensitive inference (their SLA has a 99.9% <120ms token latency clause). If we need to shift their production to a lower-risk model/quantization, ops will need 5 business days' notice.
- Adept: Medium is correct; they have lower traffic and can tolerate a short canary rollback.

I'll update the matrix with explicit SLA rows and a "notice window" column. Also: can we include a short callout for Dedicated customers who need a private rollout path? Novum will insist.

Monica
Director, Customer Success — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Two requests: 
- Keep the gating criteria crisp (3 signals max) — suggested candidates: unit-test pass rate >= 98%, perf regression delta <= 3% for p50/p95, and successful canary with no P1 errors for 48 hours.
- Provide me one example customer story (Novum) to show what a P1 vs P2 impact looks like in practice — Monica, can you provide that?

I'll draft slides by EOD Wednesday and share for review.

Subject: Re: QBR prep — Velocity signals, gating criteria, fallback playbook

Thanks — I pulled the matrix and ran it against last six sprints to produce a confidence band. Two engineering operational notes: 
1) Kernel regression: we've mitigated the root cause; perf tests are green on the feature branch, but the regression surfaced on long sequences (>= 4k) where our memory path differs. We have an infra owner assigned (PR: INF-9172).
2) Quantization toolchain: third-party library has a critical bug for some int4 repos; workaround impacts latency for Dedicated customers ~+8ms median. We can ship without it for Hosted customers and provide an opt-in private rollout for Novum.

Attached is a short playbook I authored (release_fallback_playbook.pdf) — it maps: 
- P1 (customer-facing outage): immediate rollback + hotfix lane + exec notify; owners: eng-oncall, infra-lead, CS-lead.
- P2 (degraded perf): slow-roll with throttled traffic + perf patch canary; owners: release-eng, platform.
- P3 (minor functional regressions): commit to patch in next sprint; owners: feature-area PM/eng.

Proposed canary window: 2028-07-12 00:00 PT to 2028-07-16 23:59 PT, with a mandatory 48h observation for P1 clearance. If Novum requires a private rollout, carve a dedicated canary day 2028-07-10.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR prep — Velocity signals, gating criteria, fallback playbook

Team — great progress and thank you for the concise inputs. A few final alignment points before the Thursday sync: 
- Owners: Marcus (QBR narrative + matrix), Laura (gating slide + exec bullets), Rishi (fallback playbook + canary schedule), Monica (customer impact rows + Novum contact confirmation).
- Decision thresholds accepted: unit-test >=98%, perf delta <=3%, 48h no-P1 canary window. Those are our QBR asks — we'll present them as the release controls.
- Risk callouts for the QBR: put the kernel regression as "mitigated — monitoring active" and quantization toolchain as "workaround in place, opt-in dedicated rollout for Novum".

Marcus — confirm you can assemble the final appendix (matrix + playbook links + JIRA INF-9172) by EOD Wednesday next week so we can lock the QBR deck on Friday.

I'll join Thursday 10:30 PT for the 30m review.

Vivek Kulkarni
CEO, Redwood Inference
